source_text: Non igitur quia peccaverant, genitalia vel diabolica vel inhonesta fecerunt; sed quia pavitabant, in ea qua primum fuerant honestate permanentia membra texerunt! Ideo - dicas - homines fuisse primitus nudos, quia ad sollertiae humanae operam ut se tegerent pertinebat, quae nondum in illis fuit
pass_a_gloss: Not therefore because peccaverant, genitalia or diabolica or inhonesta fecerunt; but because pavitabant, in she/it where first fuerant honestate permanentia members texerunt! for-that-reason - dicas - human-beings to-have-been primitus nudos, because to sollertiae humanae operam so-that/as himself tegerent pertinebat, which not-yet in those was.
pass_b_english: Human beings were naked at first because making coverings for themselves was a task for human skill, which they did not yet possess.

It was not, therefore, because they had sinned that they made the sexual organs either diabolical or shameful. Rather, because they were afraid, they covered organs that remained in the same honorable condition in which they had first existed.

choices.why: Augustine's quoted claim that the unbaptized remain under the devil; keep the personal devil, not 'evil'.
rejected: under Satan (name not in the Latin here)

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded. Julian is not first-English.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Contra Iulianum / Against Julian), including authorities Julian quoted; Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
